rationale: Braking execution or omission is legitimately part of P: H-1, SG-1 and FR-7 require characterising whether required braking occurs. However, the declared scope also incorporates obstacle detection and perception-generated distance information. FR-7.2, FR-7.2.4 and the architecture establish these as supporting perception functions and inputs, not as constituent behaviours of the braking-omission phenomenon. Their causal relevance to braking does not by itself establish membership in P.
determining_elements: “Braking-maneuver ... execution state” is supported target behaviour, not an overextension merely because it concerns system response.
“Including obstacle detection” explicitly adds an observation function to the phenomenon rather than treating it as a supporting mechanism.

“Distance-to-obstacle information,” grouped with detection, extends P into perception outputs; the physical obstacle distance can contextualise required braking without incorporating the mechanisms that determine it.
